Bug_Title: MF: Method defines a variable that obscures a field (MF_METHOD_MASKS_FIELD)
Bug_Details:
This method defines a local variable with the same name as a field
in this class or a superclass.  This may cause the method to
read an uninitialized value from the field, leave the field uninitialized,
or both.
Bug_Explanation: This method defines a local variable with the same name as a field in the class. This bug will cause the method to return a local variable's value instead of setting the class field.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered in the line where the showBug method is called on buggyObject. This method defines a local variable with the same name as a field in the class, causing it to return the local variable's value instead of setting the class field.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm the presence of the bug. The test method 'testShowBug' creates an instance of 'FieldMaskingBug' and sets a message using the'setMessage' method. Then, it calls the'showBug' method, which defines a local variable 'localMessage' that obscures the class field'message'. The'showBug' method returns 'localMessage', which is set to 'Buggy message'. The test asserts that the returned message is not equal to the initially set message, which it is not. This confirms that the local variable 'localMessage' is being returned instead of the class field'message', which is the expected behavior according to the bug information.
